title: mpy_ld.py: Unsupported relocation when using cos/sin functions
body: I am building dynamic native modules that use sinf/cosf with MicroPython 1.22.2 from git. Because libm and libgcc object files are not linked automatically, I extract the required objects from their archives and add them to SRC_O. Linking with tools/mpy_ld.py raises AssertionError: 11 for ARCH=xtensawin and AssertionError: 2 for ARCH=armv7emsp instead of producing a functional module. My toolchains are xtensa-esp32-elf-gcc 11.2.0 and arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2.0. This appears to happen whenever code calling sin/cos or sinf/cosf is present, even if that code path is unused, because mpy_ld.py does not appear to strip dead code. I can inspect the objects with readelf or objdump, but I do not know how to interpret why these relocations differ from the others.

symptoms_visible: When I link a dynamic native module containing sinf/cosf and the extracted libm and libgcc objects, mpy_ld.py stops with AssertionError: 11 on xtensawin and AssertionError: 2 on armv7emsp.
The exception also occurs when the code calling sin or cos exists but is not executed.
N0.label: N0 unsupported relocations reported

symptoms_visible: The original mpy_ld.py still raises unsupported-relocation assertions for these participant118module inputs.
N1.label: N1 Xtensa relocation patch tested

symptoms_visible: After updating to the new linking support, my other ARM and xtensawin builds complete, but the minimal armv6m module containing a participant20point division still stops in do_relocation_text with AssertionError: 2.
With several Ubuntu and ARM GCC packages the armv6m build raises the assertion, while one Arch Linux GCC package emits objects that the linker accepts.
A build made with the earlier simple handling for relocation type 2 crashes when I run it on the device.
N2_x.label: N2_x residual ARMv6m failure after general linking support

symptoms_visible: Building the minimal armv6m module with -fPIC still stops at the same do_relocation_text assertion for relocation type 2.
N3.label: N3 PIC model probe completed

symptoms_visible: On a MicroPython build containing the fix, armv6m native modules using participant20point division, sin and cos link successfully and run on an RP2040 without the unsupported absolute-relocation assertion.
N_terminal.label: terminal ARM absolute relocation supported

question_patterns: Can you apply this patch that recognizes R_XTENSA_ASM_EXPAND relocation 11 and test the Xtensa or xtensawin build?
Does treating Xtensa relocation type 11 like the existing DIFF32 relocations allow your module to build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, the suggested patch did help in my Xtensa case and the module build completed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The patched linker still stops on Xtensa relocation type 11 at the same assertion.
The patch works for my Xtensa test module, although I used a different module that also links math runtime objects.

edges.comment: The successful Xtensa test came from another affected user and is folded into the simulated user side. It establishes that relocation 11 needs separate Xtensa handling but does not resolve the later ARMv6m R_ARM_ABS32 case.

solution.intent: Treat the new participant118module archive linking and relocation support from issue 15838 as the complete resolution for modules that pull sin, cos and soft-float objects from libm and libgcc.
solution.concrete_example: Update MicroPython to a revision containing commit 51976110e2da32b7a5b7035b7d5f17ab49bbd40e and pass libgcc.a and libm.a directly to mpy_ld.py rather than manually maintaining every extracted object.

edges.comment: The reporter updated emlearn-micropython to the new linking support. It fixed almost all original cases, including the other ARM and xtensawin targets, but a minimal armv6m participant20point division still triggered relocation type 2. Thus this was necessary infrastructure but not a complete resolution.

question_patterns: Can you rebuild the armv6m module with -fPIC instead of -fpic and report whether the relocation changes?
Please try the non-optimized PIC memory model and paste the resulting linker error, if any.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried building the module with -fPIC, and I still get caught on the same assertion due to the absolute relocation: AssertionError: 2.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With -fPIC the armv6m module links and runs correctly, and relocation type 2 no longer appears.
The -fPIC build still produces relocation type 2, but the failing offset is in a different libgcc object.

edges.comment: This is a handler-requested compiler-flag probe, so it is a measurement clarification. The raw outcome rules out changing only the PIC model; identifying relocation 2 as R_ARM_ABS32 and determining how to support it remain engineer-side conclusions.

solution.intent: Add correct R_ARM_ABS32 relocation support for ARM text sections by reusing mpy_ld.py's existing absolute-relocation logic for read-only data, then update to the MicroPython revision containing that fix and verify the native math module on armv6m hardware.
solution.concrete_example: Update to a MicroPython revision containing commit 718ff4fdd58efd3e853599b489640877070d17be. The change allows R_ARM_ABS32 relocations in a text section to use the already-supported ro-data relocation path, covering addresses of float constant tables used by sin/cos and ARM soft-float routines. Please rebuild and run the minimal division and sin/cos modules on the RP2040 and report the values before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied raw AssertionError: 2 output, object/link logs, compiler-package comparisons and the failed -fPIC result. Engineers identified type 2 as R_ARM_ABS32, observed that the relevant relocation points at data embedded in a text section, and recognized that mpy_ld.py's existing ro-data relocation implementation could safely handle the same case. Those conclusions must not be presented as facts the reporter already knew.

edges.comment: Final resolution from PR 17377 and commit 718ff4fdd58efd3e853599b489640877070d17be. The implemented fix supports an ldr from a PC-relative literal location whose stored word has R_ARM_ABS32, including float constant-table addresses used by sin/cos on armv6m.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the remaining root cause as R_ARM_ABS32 relocations attached to data in ARM text sections, such as addresses of participant20point constant tables used by sin/cos and soft-float routines; the assertion number alone is not a sufficient diagnosis.
Must ground the diagnosis in the armv6m minimal participant20point-division reproduction, compiler-dependent object output, and the unchanged relocation after the -fPIC probe.
Must recommend the implemented fix: handle R_ARM_ABS32 in text sections using the existing ro-data absolute-relocation logic, available in commit 718ff4fdd58efd3e853599b489640877070d17be.
Must not treat issue 15838 or the earlier simplistic ARM absolute-relocation calculation as the complete fix: the former left armv6m failing, and a module built with the latter crashed on-device.
Must not present switching from -fpic to -fPIC as the fix because the reporter tested it and still received AssertionError: 2.
Must ask the user to rebuild and run the division or sin/cos module on an armv6m build containing the fix, and only treat the issue as resolved after successful runtime verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced embedded and MicroPython developer who maintains participant118module build files, extracts runtime objects from static archives, compares cross-compiler packages, produces minimal reproductions, and can test linker patches on hardware, but is not deeply familiar with ELF relocation semantics.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, methodical and collaborative; supplies complete commands and verbose logs, distinguishes architectures and toolchain versions carefully, and openly states uncertainty when interpreting low-level linker output.
